title: 3. Qualifications and Disqualifications of Lok Sabha Members

blocks.content: A person shall not be qualified to be chosen to fill a seat in Parliament unless he is a citizen of India and is, in the case of a seat in the House of the People, not less than twenty-five years of age.

rows: Office of profit, unsound mind, insolvency, non-citizenship
Defection, voting against party mandate, voluntarily giving up membership
Mandatory advice from the Election Commission
Subject to Judicial Review (Kihoto Hollohan case, 1992)

items: Notice the age difference: Minimum age for Lok Sabha is 25 years, whereas for Rajya Sabha it is 30 years.
Disqualification under Article 102 is decided by the President on the advice of the Election Commission, whereas disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is decided by the Speaker.
A person convicted under RPA 1951 with 2+ years of imprisonment remains disqualified for the sentence period plus an additional six years after release.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 84 prescribes that a Lok Sabha member must be a citizen of India, at least 25 years of age, and make an oath/affirmation prescribed in the Third Schedule.
Article 102 outlines constitutional disqualifications including holding an office of profit, being of unsound mind, being an undischarged insolvent, or losing Indian citizenship.
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 specifies statutory disqualifications, such as conviction for an offense resulting in imprisonment for two or more years.
Disqualification on grounds of defection is governed separately under the Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.
